one_line: Collaborative collection of diverse personal-agent answers to big questions
what_it_does: Users publish questions and participants ask their personal agents to submit independent, anonymous answers revealed together.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides a structured submission and retrieval boundary for many independent personal agents, making a shared asynchronous answer pool more reliable than UI automation.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes one-answer-per-participant WebMCP submission and private-until-reveal state.
execution_rationale: The concept and core flow are coherent, but the packet gives no transcript and only frame-sheet evidence is available for the end-to-end interaction.
execution_evidence: Video frame sheets are supplied as authoritative product-motion evidence; ABOUT describes draft, publish, deadline, submission, and reveal states.
impact_rationale: A real use case for collective reflection and deliberation is clearly articulated; diverse independent perspectives are the point rather than consensus.
impact_evidence: ABOUT identifies societal and everyday questions and anonymous independent responses.
creativity_rationale: Personal agents as distinct perspectives in a timed reveal is a fresh, memorable social interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Pitch centers on agents carrying different user context and independent answers.
usability_note: The workflow is understandable and likely usable, though participation depends on bringing a personal agent into the flow.
standouts: Strong framing of diversity without voting or forced consensus.
advance_reason: Strong concept and meaningful multi-agent collaboration; end-to-end evidence is adequate but not richly documented.

one_line: A shared browser design canvas operated concurrently by a person and an AI agent
what_it_does: A forked design editor lets a human select live objects while an agent edits the same canvas through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes live in-memory design objects and human selection state directly, enabling semantic co-editing that brittle UI automation cannot reproduce comparably well.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT explicitly says the agent sees actual selected objects and operates on live application state.
execution_rationale: The central collaborative editing workflow is clearly specified and the video frame sheets provide product-motion evidence, though transcript detail is absent.
execution_evidence: Video frame sheets; ABOUT describes real-time design actions, selection, and multi-version poster work.
impact_rationale: Designers have a concrete repetitive-work problem and the editor directly addresses localization, alignment, resizing, and variants.
impact_evidence: ABOUT names platform variants, translated headlines, grids, and brand recoloring.
creativity_rationale: Shared-canvas human/agent editing with selection-aware commands is an unusually strong interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Pitch and ABOUT emphasize simultaneous operation and semantic selection.
usability_note: The shared canvas and direct manipulation model are compelling; complexity of agent instruction remains a usability consideration.
standouts: Best demonstration of WebMCP changing what an agent can understand about UI state.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP leverage and a deeply specific human-agent design workflow.

one_line: A constrained course planner that makes long-term tradeoffs and personal limits explicit
what_it_does: Students plan courses through tools that explain opportunity costs, enforce user-set constraints, and support undo/audit.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools maintain plan state, constraints, refusal semantics, and replayable events; a general UI agent would be less reliable and could violate the student boundary.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes thirteen tools, stateful refusal, locked user constraint, event log, and replay-based undo.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent central workflow from planning through refusal, repair, and undo; frame sheets support product motion despite no transcript.
execution_evidence: Video frame sheets; ABOUT gives concrete NUM-201 refusal and plan replay flow.
impact_rationale: Students have a real high-stakes planning problem and the explicit opportunity-cost and self-protection model provides credible value.
impact_evidence: ABOUT describes credits, specializations, two-year consequences, and user-owned limits.
creativity_rationale: The product treats refusal, auditability, and user constraints as first-class planning interactions rather than generic course search.
creativity_evidence: Pitch and ABOUT emphasize tools refusing and explaining what choices close off.
usability_note: The prose-first refusal and audit model should make complex plans legible; initial setup may be demanding.
standouts: Strong constraint-aware planning model; tool descriptions are treated as product surface.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP/stateful safety design paired with a credible student need.

one_line: Human-supervised volunteer dispatch and conflict repair
what_it_does: An agent drafts and validates volunteer assignments while a coordinator retains approval, locked decisions, and sensitive-contact control.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the dispatcher structured access to schedules, assignments, validation, and audit state while preserving explicit human authority.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT lists read/create/validate/repair/prepare/commit tools and forbidden actions.
execution_rationale: The packet lays out a complete draft-conflict-repair-approval workflow with visible human control; frame sheets are product-motion evidence.
execution_evidence: Video frame sheets; ABOUT gives R-105/R-106 conflict and locked assignment scenario.
impact_rationale: Volunteer coordinators have a concrete scheduling and safety problem, and the demo addresses it without removing accountability.
impact_evidence: ABOUT describes eight requests, five volunteers, coordinator edits, conflict explanation, and repair.
creativity_rationale: The human-in-the-loop dispatcher is a thoughtful synthesis of scheduling automation and governance.
creativity_evidence: Pitch and ABOUT emphasize preserving coordinator control.
usability_note: Clear staged workflow and bounded permissions; fictional data limits demonstrated operational breadth.
standouts: Conflict preservation and repair around a locked human choice.
advance_reason: Strong, credible safety-oriented dispatcher with a well-defined end-to-end scenario.

one_line: Governance console that authorizes, denies, or escalates WebMCP actions
what_it_does: A browser tool surface routes agent requests through an independent policy boundary before protected disclosure or publication.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the capability surface while the governance layer determines authority, making permission decisions explicit and independently enforced.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes inspect_document and publish_document crossing a host boundary into Ananke decisions.
execution_rationale: The narrow demonstration covers allow, approval, and deny paths and is presented with video frame sheets, though no transcript is supplied.
execution_evidence: Video frame sheets; ABOUT describes fixed document, host boundary, and three decisions.
impact_rationale: Agent governance and human approval are real needs for anyone exposing browser capabilities, and the product makes the boundary legible.
impact_evidence: ABOUT identifies protected data disclosure and host-side action risks.
creativity_rationale: The Fates/Ananke model is a crisp and memorable governance framing for WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Pitch and ABOUT distinguish capability discovery from authority.
usability_note: Small tool surface makes the policy flow easy to understand; broader policy authoring is not demonstrated.
standouts: Clear separation of capability and authority.
advance_reason: Strong governance concept with credible narrow implementation and evidence.

one_line: Human-attributed participatory neighborhood budgeting with agent assistance
what_it_does: An agent gathers state, simulates and proposes allocations, explains tradeoffs, and requests human review without an adoption tool.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP structures shared budget state, validation, simulation, tradeoffs, and review while deliberately omitting the consequential adoption action.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT lists seven tools, machine-readable violations, revision state, and no tool to adopt.
execution_rationale: The budget workflow and human decision boundary are concrete and comprehensive; frame sheets support motion evidence.
execution_evidence: Video frame sheets; ABOUT describes eight works, fixed fund, invalid drafts, and named human review.
impact_rationale: Participatory budgeting is a real civic decision with a clear audience and the product supports informed, attributable choice.
impact_evidence: ABOUT grounds the scenario in resident budgeting and named human decision-making.
creativity_rationale: The interaction model makes non-delegation a structural product feature and connects agent assistance to civic deliberation.
creativity_evidence: Pitch and ABOUT emphasize no adoption tool and contestability.
usability_note: Rich explanations and validation should help residents; civic budgeting domain knowledge may raise onboarding cost.
standouts: Structural boundary around adoption is unusually principled.
advance_reason: High-impact civic workflow with transformative structured assistance and a strong concept.

one_line: A private browser-based structured research outline that agents can inspect and improve
what_it_does: Users organize sources and typed relationships locally, then let agents read and suggest changes through WebMCP for human review.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides structured access to a local research graph without login, plugin, or server setup, making agent collaboration more reliable than scraping an outline.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes typed hierarchy, links/notes, WebMCP reading and suggestions, and human approval.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a developed editor concept and video frame sheets, but the available description does not establish every end-to-end editing state.
execution_evidence: Video frame sheets; ABOUT describes example pages, outline editor, and suggestion review.
impact_rationale: Researchers and knowledge workers have a credible need for private structured notes and agent-assisted synthesis.
impact_evidence: ABOUT describes private browser data, sources, relationships, and agent improvements.
creativity_rationale: The portable typed research graph and human-reviewed agent suggestions are a useful synthesis, though adjacent to existing outliners.
creativity_evidence: ABOUT describes portable Swift kernel and WebAssembly reader.
usability_note: Clear outline structure and local-first privacy are useful; type hierarchy may require learning.
standouts: Local-first structured research with no plugin/server setup.
advance_reason: Solid research tool with meaningful WebMCP integration; novelty and evidence are good but not exceptional.

one_line: A human-controlled inquiry-call planner that lets ChatGPT prepare a disclosed information-only call
what_it_does: The agent creates a structured call plan; a person confirms, a voice worker makes one bounded call, and the result returns as an auditable receipt.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP bridges conversation to a structured plan and returned call result while intentionally withholding confirmation and commitment authority from the agent.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT explicitly says confirmation is absent from the WebMCP tools and results are structured per question with receipt metadata.
execution_rationale: The packet specifies a complete plan-confirm-call-result loop and supplies product-motion frame sheets, though no transcript is available.
execution_evidence: Video frame sheets; ABOUT describes destination, questions, limits, confirmation, call, and receipt.
impact_rationale: Avoiding unwanted phone calls is a common real-life pain point, and information-only calls with disclosure and limits provide credible value.
impact_evidence: ABOUT lists hotels, accessibility, bills, delivery windows, and translation use cases.
creativity_rationale: Combining conversational planning, bounded voice action, and explicit human authority is distinctive and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Pitch and ABOUT emphasize one disclosed information-only call and no commitment actions.
usability_note: The staged plan and receipt support trust; requiring sign-in and phone permissions adds friction.
standouts: Strong consequential-action boundary; useful bridge from chat to real-world phone inquiry.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-value workflow with strong safety and structured WebMCP leverage.

one_line: Invoice exception review where an agent stages evidence and a person decides payment action
what_it_does: The agent reads a payable queue and stages a permitted resolution draft; a human confirms or dismisses it.
leverage_rationale: Structured invoice evidence, variance checks, and draft staging are materially safer and more reliable than having an agent infer a dense dashboard, while payment remains human-only.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes two tools, exact $200 variance evidence, allowed actions, and no payment/contact authority.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a concrete two-invoice run and visible draft boundary, with frame sheets as product-motion evidence.
execution_evidence: Video frame sheets; ABOUT describes PP-2086, $119 versus $94, and credit-and-hold draft.
impact_rationale: Accounts-payable reviewers have a specific costly error-detection problem and the deterministic evidence plus staged resolution addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: ABOUT identifies an exact invoice discrepancy and supporting evidence.
creativity_rationale: A focused and credible safety pattern, though invoice review is a familiar category and the scope is intentionally narrow.
creativity_evidence: Pitch and ABOUT describe deterministic checks separated from agent actions.
usability_note: The evidence-first draft makes review actionable; small fictional queue limits breadth.
standouts: Excellent separation of deterministic checks, agent staging, and human payment decision.
advance_reason: Strong practical finance workflow with clear evidence and a sound authority boundary.

one_line: A 3v3 pixel-art cat soccer game with a bounded semantic AI sideline coach
what_it_does: Players play a local arcade match while an agent reads match state and issues tactical, formation, and role instructions without raw control.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes semantic game state and bounded tactical actions while preserving simulation legality and player agency; raw keypress automation is explicitly excluded.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT lists 23 tools, semantic orders, live state, causality trace, and bounded utility-AI effects.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete playable match and coach loop with visible causality tracing; frame sheets provide product-motion evidence.
execution_evidence: Video frame sheets; ABOUT describes match state, formations, tactics, orders, and control modes.
impact_rationale: Players who want an AI-assisted tactical arcade experience have a clear entertainment use case, and the game visibly addresses safe agent control.
impact_evidence: ABOUT describes 3v3 cat football, human play, local AI, and coach opt-in.
creativity_rationale: Semantic coaching that preserves agency is a strong interaction design beyond generic game automation.
creativity_evidence: Pitch and ABOUT contrast semantic directives with raw keys, physics, and score mutation.
usability_note: Coach opt-in, bounded orders, and causality trace support learnability and trust; game state still has inherent complexity.
standouts: Strong semantic-action boundary and unusually legible causality trace.
advance_reason: Ambitious playable game concept with meaningful WebMCP control rather than keypress automation.
